L0@P0: UTCVM ONCOLOGY & CLINICAL PATHOLOGY SERVICES CLINICAL TRIAL
L1@P0: It’s All In the Genes: The Genetic Landscape
L2@P0: of Acute Myeloid Leukemia in Dogs
L3@P0: Purpose of study
L4@P0: Acute myeloid leukemia is a devastating blood cancer that
L5@P0: is rapidly fatal, with most dogs succumbing within 2 months.
L6@P0: Currently in veterinary medicine, we have few ways of treating
L7@P0: this leukemia and know little about the underlying genetic
L8@P0: defects. In people, genetic analysis has revolutionized treatment
L9@P0: of acute myeloid leukemia, with drugs being developed to
L10@P0: target the primary underlying genetic abnormality. We are
L11@P0: working to make that possible in veterinary medicine, too,
L12@P0: but we need knowledge of the genetic abnormalities that are
L13@P0: responsible for the leukemia.
L14@P0: Eligibility criteria
L15@P0: Dogs with a diagnosis of acute leukemia based on CBC with
L16@P0: blood smear evaluation, or bone marrow cytology.
L17@P0: Study details
L18@P0: We ask to collect a small amount of blood and a mouth swab for DNA with owner’s informed consent. There are no
L19@P0: further obligations or responsibilities. Please contact the referral coordinator to refer your patient to the oncology
L20@P0: service for clients seeking treatment for acute leukemia. If treatment is not desired, your patient may participate in
L21@P0: the study remotely. We will send you a sample collection kit, consent form, and prepaid shipping label.
L22@P0: Study benefits & cost
L23@P0: The study will pay for flow cytometry analysis of blood or bone marrow to confirm acute myeloid versus lymphoid
L24@P0: leukemia. We will sequence the genes of the tumor cells in your patient to discover which ones are abnormal and
L25@P0: potentially responsible for the tumor. While your patient may not directly benefit from this study, studies like this
L26@P0: represent the future of medicine and are needed to improve the diagnosis and treatment of disease.
L27@P0: There is no cost to be involved in this study, which is funded through the American Kennel Club Canine Health
L28@P0: Foundation. Your client will be responsible for other costs of their dog’s visit, however the study is paying to
L29@P0: confirm that the leukemia in your patient is acute myeloid leukemia (versus acute lymphoid leukemia or Stage V
L30@P0: lymphoma).
L31@P0: Think you have an eligible patient?
L32@P0: Nora Springer, DVM, PhD, DACVP (Primary Investigator) | nspringer@utk.edu
L33@P0: This study is IACUC-approved (#2893-0222).
